newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU refinery output falls sharply in March - Euroil.
newsitem.headline: EU refinery output falls sharply in March - Euroil.

text.p: Refinery output in the European Union fell by 5.7 percent in March, with distillate production down by over nine percent, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

Total refinery output in the European Union, excluding Sweden, fell by 684,000 barrels per day (bpd) (5.7 percent) to 11,302 million bpd in March, while refinery crude intake was down 823,000 bpd (7.2 percent) to 10,685 million bpd. This represented a utilisation rate of 84.80 percent, against 91.33 percent in February.
But year-on-year, total output was up 73,000 bpd (0.7 percent).
Middle distillate output was down 502,000 bpd (9.1 percent) in March to 5,017 million bpd.
Gasoline production fell 116,000 bpd (3.6 percent) in March to 3,075 million bpd, but was 84,000 bpd (2.8 percent) more than a year ago.
Fuel oil output dipped by 25,000 bpd (1.4 percent) to 1,708 million bpd which was 35,000 bpd (2.1 percent) more than a year ago.
Naphtha output was down 56,000 bpd (5.5 percent) to 965,000 bpd, 73,000 bpd (8.2 percent) higher than in March 1996.
They are based on a nameplate capacity of 12.6 million bpd. Refinery intake represents crude only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
